checks: On the compact product, the scaled product of the normalized marginals has mass M and the right marginals. The marginal equalities are weakly closed. Separate Lipschitz bounds imply joint continuity by telescoping over the coordinates.

The Voronoi construction covers each support within δ/2 and every representative owns an open relative δ/4-neighborhood, so the normalized restrictions for lifting are valid. Finite LP duality has the correct signs: primal maximum, dual minimum, sum of potentials ≥ cost.

Each one-coordinate maximum replaces only that potential by a feasible pointwise minorant and forces its L_i-Lipschitz bound. Weak duality prevents the objective from dropping below optimum. The zero-total-sum normalization and an equality tuple of positive optimal array mass bound the final potential too; this works when k=1.

The Lipschitz extension agrees at each representative. Comparing both cost and summed potentials with the representative tuple gives possible deficit 2δΣ_iL_i. Collapsing and lifting bound the primal-value error in both directions by MδΣ_iL_i; the marginal-integral error from extending and adding the feasibility shift is at most 3MδΣ_iL_i. A common uniform subsequence on the finitely many supports passes feasibility and value to the limit.

The full K_i extensions use minimizers t_i on the compact supports; Σ_i u_i(x_i) ≥ c(t)+Σ_i L_i|x_i−t_i| ≥ c(x). They preserve the integrals. The nonnegative integrated dual gap vanishes for any minimizing potentials paired with any maximizing coupling.
